The ZIP is unencrypted. Do not use it for passwords or other secrets.
Save the current clipboard as a clip with one tap — other content is shared into the app via Share → KlipSilo.
Use the search field and the type filter to find clips fast.
Double-tap the URL icon to open it in a browser, or the location icon to open navigation.
Rename clips from the action sheet (except Location). Locked clips cannot be renamed either.
Duplicate a clip to create a new one with the same content — files are copied.
Tap the pin to keep important clips at the top of the list. Tap again to unpin.

Choose \"Lock/unlock\" in the action sheet to protect a clip. A locked clip shows a padlock next to its pin and cannot be deleted, renamed or edited — and it is skipped when deleting under Maintenance. Everything else still works: View content, Share, conversions and Duplicate. Unlock in the same place.
Delete clips with an undo option — you can also delete a whole type under Maintenance. Locked clips cannot be deleted.

Tap a clip to open it. Long-press the clip, or tap ⋮, for the action sheet: View content, Share, Save to Downloads, conversions, Rename, Duplicate, Lock/unlock and Delete. On locked clips, Rename, Delete and Text editor are dimmed.
On text and PDF clips you can find URLs and phone numbers and open or call them.
File clips can be converted to PDF or plain text (txt, rtf, docx, xlsx) — unknown formats can be tried as text, and docx/xlsx/rtf are shown directly as readable text.
Zoom with two fingers and pan when zoomed in. Pages start at 1x.
Use the arrows to switch pages, save a single page as its own PDF, or extract a page\'s images as new image clips.
The QR button reads QR codes on the page — copy the message, save it as a clip, or open it directly in the text editor.
Run OCR on the current page or the whole PDF to extract the text.
Create a text clip and go straight into the editor — save with the checkmark. The editor has undo/redo, adjustable text size (A−/A+) and its own PDF button.
Create a clip with your current address. The app explains why it needs location before asking, and you can refuse and still use everything else.
Combine PDFs or combine text clips — mark the order with numbers.
Add text, draw straight lines or freehand strokes, and save a new PDF from the top bar.

Delete clips by type — or all of them — with an undo option. Locked clips are not counted and are not deleted. Save all clips as a zip file via \"Backup clips\" and choose the location yourself (e.g. Google Drive). The filename includes the date. \"Restore clips\" loads one or more previously saved zip files — new clips are added, nothing is overwritten, and pin/lock status and timestamps are preserved.
Read QR codes with the camera, and run OCR from the camera, an image clip, or a PDF — when scanning images you can also save a cropped selection as an image clip.
Switch language and choose display mode (System, Light, Dark) — only for KlipSilo.
Set margin, font size, line spacing and the maximum output resolution for text-to-PDF.

The file-to-PDF conversion faithfully reproduces the document — text, headings, images, tables and list markers — but it is a simplified rendering, not a 1:1 copy of the Word layout. Here are the known cosmetic limitations and what they mean in practice:
The font is not the document\'s own
The document\'s font (e.g. Arial or Calibri) is replaced by a standard font. The text is easy to read, but line breaks may fall a little differently than in Word.
Words are not necessarily broken at the same places as in the original document. There is no hyphenation, and justified text is rendered left-aligned.
The space between paragraphs is a fixed standard distance, not necessarily the one the author chose in the document.
Cells with merged columns or rows (colspan/rowspan) are rendered as ordinary cells. Column widths are estimated from the content and may differ from the original. Borders are uniform.
Headers and footers (e.g. page numbers and document name) from the original document are omitted.

Floating images and text boxes are rendered in the text flow instead of at their exact position in the document, so text and images may appear elsewhere than in Word. The worst artifacts, e.g. stray single letters from text boxes, are filtered out automatically.
Lists have markers but no indentation
Numbered lists and bullet lists get correct markers (1., 2., • etc.), but without indentation — they look like ordinary paragraphs with a character in front.
If the original document itself contains the same image several times (e.g. copied drawings), it appears several times in the PDF. That is faithful to the source, but can look like an error.
Fonts such as Wingdings and Symbol are mapped to ordinary characters via a limited table. Rare special characters may therefore be shown as a different character.

The content — text, images and structure — is fully readable and can be selected and searched in the PDF. The deviations are cosmetic: typography, line breaks, spacing and the position of floating elements come close to the original, but are not identical to it.

KlipSilo is a clipboard, not an office suite. Everything in the app is designed around one idea: content you want to keep should be easy to find, view and reuse — without you having to think about where it came from.
Why clips are saved when you save them

KlipSilo does not monitor your clipboard in the background — modern Android does not allow apps to do that (privacy). Capture is deliberate and explicit: content enters the app when you choose it. Use Share → KlipSilo in any app, or tap "Save current clipboard" in the app to save exactly what is on your clipboard right now. Nothing is captured without your knowledge — but you do have to share or save what you want to keep.

Text, links, images, PDFs, files and places behave differently — a link should open in a browser, a PDF should be browsed, a place should be shown on a map. Giving each clip a type lets the app know what makes sense to do with it and shows only the relevant actions.
Why the action sheet gathers everything

All actions for a clip live in one place: view, share, convert, rename, duplicate and delete. That makes the app predictable — you never have to search for functions; they are always in the same menu.
Why conversions never touch the original

When you convert (for example docx to PDF), a new clip is always created — the original is untouched. "Convert" means "make a new version", not "replace". You can compare, delete or try again without any risk.
Why the text editor behaves as it does

The checkmark saves and stays — saving is something you do along the way, not the end of the work; you leave with the back arrow. The name only changes when you rename it, because the name is your label for finding the clip. Undo/redo and text size with proportional line spacing make editing forgiving — and the PDF button creates a PDF that matches exactly what you see.
Why file→PDF is rendered in the app itself

The conversion builds the PDF directly in the app without external engines. Text becomes real PDF text (searchable and selectable), images are embedded, and tables and lists are rendered. It works offline, quickly and consistently — but it is a simplified rendering: typography and layout come close to the original without being identical. That is why the Limitations page exists: honesty about what to expect.
Why documents are shown as text

docx/xlsx/rtf files are not opened in a document app — they are shown as extracted text. A clipboard is about content, not about editing the document. The text gives you quick access to what matters, while the file stays untouched and can be converted whenever you want.
Why the PDF viewer has exactly these tools

Zoom, page browsing, OCR, QR reading and "save page as PDF" — chosen because PDFs in a clipboard context are usually for reference and reuse: read a page, extract the text, read a code, or save a single page for later.
Why the settings are split up

Language and display are about how the app looks to you. The PDF settings are about what the output should be used for (margin, font size, line spacing, resolution). They are separate because "how I read" and "what the PDF should be like" are two different choices.
Why the Guide is part of the app

Tips and limitations live in the app because a good app does not hide its design: Tips tells you what is possible, Limitations tells you honestly what is not. Then you can use the app with realistic expectations — and that is a user guide in itself.

KlipSilo is a clipboard that saves, organises and reuses what you copy — and can convert documents to PDF. Here are the situations where the app makes a real difference:
Copied text, links and images from email, browser, messages and apps are saved in one place — ideal for research, studies and projects where you collect notes from many places.
TXT, RTF, DOCX and XLSX files can be converted to a readable PDF directly in the app — with text, headings, images, tables and list markers. No external programs and no internet needed.
Convert DOCX user guides (for example for medical devices or applications) to PDF, browse them, zoom into details, and extract the text with OCR if it is locked in images.
Open PDFs in the app: browse pages, zoom with two fingers, decode QR codes on a page, run OCR to extract text, and save a single page as its own PDF.
Add text and draw strokes (straight line or free hand) on a PDF — useful for marking important sections, filling in fields or highlighting something before sharing the document.
Links and phone numbers in text and PDFs can be found automatically and opened directly — handy for contact details, booking pages or customer enquiries.
Save an address or your current location as a clip and get navigation with a double-tap.
Clips can be shared, and files, PDFs and images can be saved directly to the phone\'s Downloads folder — without going through other apps.
On the device, with a few exceptions

Conversion, text extraction, OCR, QR scanning and viewing run on the phone and do not use a KlipSilo server. Content is only shared when you do it yourself. Saving a location may look up an address via the device geocoder (usually Google). Android backup does not restore clips — export a ZIP from the app if you want a copy.
Simple operation with few, clear actions. Text can be enlarged in the editor, the display can be set to light or dark mode, and the whole app can run in Danish.

KlipSilo uses your current location only when you tap Location. The coordinates are stored as a clip on this device. To show an address, the coordinates may be sent to your device\'s geocoding service (usually Google on phones with Google Play). KlipSilo has no servers and does not show ads. You can deny this and still use the rest of the app.
